reason: Both conversations correctly started with the unplug-and-turn-the-drum check and honestly declined to name an exact belt part on a partial 'TVHM8' model, ultimately pointing to an engineer. Conversation 1 went further and more usefully: it used the customer's willingness to remove the back panel (with power isolated), got visual confirmation of the snapped belt lying in the base, and prompted a check of the tensioner arm, aligning with the jockey-pulley concern in the expected diagnosis. Conversation 2 spent its opener on an overload question, never reached visual confirmation, hedged that 'testing would be needed', and offered no DIY path despite a textbook snapped-belt presentation. Conversation 1's closing refusal to let the customer measure the belt and its 'fire risk' framing were over-cautious, but it still delivered a fuller, confirmed diagnosis.
